title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: classify Azure RMS protected Office files on Windows (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The roadmap facts, licensing, navigation paths and path-exclusion command are supported. The just-in-time blocking description should acknowledge the more specific conditions in Microsoft's detailed guide, and the checklist names controls missing from the table.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope; rationales
claims.claim: The roadmap plans Endpoint DLP classification of Office files with Azure RMS protection.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP can now classify Office files stored in Windows devices that have Azure RMS protection applied.

claims.claim: The capability concerns files stored on Windows devices.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP can now classify Office files stored in Windows devices that have Azure RMS protection applied.

claims.claim: Classification is triggered when the file is used in applications.
claims.quote: Classification will be triggered when file is used in applications or when just-in-time classification is enabled.

claims.claim: The roadmap also identifies enabling just-in-time classification as a classification trigger.
claims.quote: Classification will be triggered when file is used in applications or when just-in-time classification is enabled.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this RMS-protected Office classification capability.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP Azure RMS protected Office files Windows classification default setting'; '"Endpoint DLP" "Azure RMS" switch classification'. Opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about, dlp-configure-endpoint-settings and the diagnostic-log guide; results describe background, not this capability.

claims.claim: The Endpoint DLP overview says files are fully scanned for sensitive information types and labels whenever created or modified.
claims.quote: Every time a file is created or modified, it is fully scanned for sensitive information types (SITs) and labels.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationales
claims.claim: Classified files are evaluated against DLP policies and rules.
claims.quote: The file is then evaluated for matches against DLP policies and rules.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft's diagnostic-log guide still says DLP cannot evaluate password-protected or encrypted files.
claims.quote: If the RMS status value is 0x1, the protected file has a password or is encrypted. DLP can't evaluate password-protected or encrypted files.

claims.claim: The roadmap description and the diagnostic-log guide disagree for RMS-protected Office files.
claims.quote: DLP can't evaluate password-protected or encrypted files.

claims.claim: Devices used as locations in DLP policies must be onboarded.
claims.quote: You need to onboard all the devices you want to use as locations in your DLP policies.

claims.claim: Device monitoring for JIT is configured in Microsoft Purview portal at Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection > Choose which locations to monitor > Devices.
claims.quote: Select Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection. Under Choose which locations to monitor, select the checkbox next to Devices.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document automation for the JIT device-monitoring setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Set-PolicyConfig EndpointDlpGlobalSettings just-in-time protection Devices fallback action API PowerShell'; '"Endpoint DLP" "just-in-time" "PowerShell" "fallback"'. Opened Set-PolicyConfig and both JIT guides; no JIT device-monitoring call found.

claims.claim: JIT requires antimalware client version 4.18.23080 or later before deployment.
claims.quote: Before you can deploy just-in-time protection, you must first deploy antimalware Client version 4.18.23080 or later.

claims.claim: Administrators should allow at least an hour for JIT setting updates to reach client devices.
claims.quote: Allow at least an hour for JIT setting updates, including disabling JIT, to be pushed to client devices.

claims.claim: The JIT fallback action is at Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection > Fallback action in case of failure.
claims.quote: Select Settings > Data Loss Prevention > Just-in-time protection. Under Fallback action in case of failure, select Allow users to complete actions.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document automation for the JIT fallback-action setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Set-PolicyConfig EndpointDlpGlobalSettings just-in-time protection Devices fallback action API PowerShell'; '"Endpoint DLP" "just-in-time" "PowerShell" "fallback"'. Opened Set-PolicyConfig and both JIT guides; no fallback-action call found.

claims.claim: The fallback choices are Allow users to complete actions and Block users from completing actions.
claims.quote: Selecting Allow users to complete actions or Block users from completing actions doesn't change whether JIT Block is triggered.

claims.claim: The fallback setting controls Endpoint DLP enforcement when classification fails.
claims.quote: The Allow users to complete actions or Block users from completing actions setting controls Endpoint DLP enforcement when classification fails.

claims.claim: Changing the fallback action does not change whether JIT Block is triggered.
claims.quote: Selecting Allow users to complete actions or Block users from completing actions doesn't change whether JIT Block is triggered.

claims.claim: Windows file path exclusions are at Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > File path exclusions for Windows.
claims.quote: To configure path exclusions in DLP settings, go to Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > File path exclusions for Windows.

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig -EndpointDlpGlobalSettings @(@{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="<file path>"}) configures global endpoint path exclusions.
claims.quote: The EndpointDlpGlobalSettings parameter specifies the global endpoints. Example values: @{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="C:\Windows";}

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig is a Security & Compliance PowerShell cmdlet.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[2].scope and note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Centrally configured endpoint settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.
claims.quote: Centrally configured settings control many aspects of endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) behavior. These settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.

claims.claim: Windows file path exclusions prevent Endpoint DLP classification and protection in the excluded paths.
claims.quote: File path exclusions for Windows setting prevents Purview from applying Endpoint DLP classification and protection for files under the specified folders.

claims.claim: JIT file path exclusions are narrower than global Windows file path exclusions because other Endpoint DLP classification and protection still apply.
claims.quote: File path exclusions in JIT only excludes specific file paths from JIT protection. In all other cases, Microsoft Purview still applies Endpoint DLP classification and protection for files in those folders.

claims.where: controls[3].ui and api; Governance controls; Why it matters
claims.claim: No separate UI switch or automation for classifying Azure RMS-protected Office files is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Endpoint DLP" "Azure RMS" switch classification'; 'Endpoint DLP Azure RMS protected Office files Windows classification default setting'. Opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about, dlp-configure-endpoint-settings, Set-PolicyConfig and JIT guides; no RMS-specific setting found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether this RMS classification capability is on by default or requires a setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP Azure RMS protected Office files Windows classification default setting'; '"Endpoint DLP" "Azure RMS" switch classification'. Read the roadmap and opened the Endpoint DLP overview, endpoint settings and JIT guides; none states this capability's default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Endpoint DLP is included in the Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Purview suite and Information Protection & Governance plans named in the service description.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection & Governance | Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) | Included

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No separate licensing requirement for this RMS classification capability is published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP Azure RMS protected Office classification licensing meter pricing'. Opened the Microsoft Purview service description; its Endpoint DLP table states Included, with no separate RMS-classification entry. Search results name no capability-specific licence or meter.

claims.claim: With JIT on, Endpoint DLP blocks egress activities on monitored files until policy evaluation completes.
claims.quote: Just-in-time protection blocks egress activities on these monitored files until policy evaluation completes successfully: Items that have never been evaluated. Items on which the evaluation has gone stale.
claims.fix: Replace that clause with 'Just-in-time protection can block egress activities while policy evaluation completes; the detailed JIT guide qualifies blocking by user scope, applicable Block or Block with override rules, allowed destinations, resume support and evaluation time.' The overview gives the broad statement, but acknowledge the more specific account at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about-jit#how-jit-protection-works, already cited in sources.

claims.claim: Disable classification excludes specified file extensions from Endpoint DLP content scanning.
claims.quote: Use this setting to exclude specific file extensions from Endpoint DLP classification. When you add a file extension to this setting, Endpoint DLP doesn't scan content in files with this extension.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout; controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist names device DLP rules and activity explorer, but neither has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: List the device DLP rules that use Block or Block with override... Watch activity explorer for new rule matches... The table contains only JIT monitoring, JIT fallback, Windows path exclusions and the absent RMS-specific switch.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullets beginning 'List the device DLP rules', 'Watch activity explorer' and 'Compare blocks on protected Office files'; these steps ask readers to review or adjust controls without table rows. Do not add rows as part of this correction.

claims.claim: No meter is documented for this RMS classification capability.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP Azure RMS protected Office classification licensing meter pricing'. Opened the Microsoft Purview service description and read its Endpoint DLP section; no RMS-classification meter is stated there or in relevant search results.

claims.claim: JIT protection supports Windows 10, Windows 11 and macOS.
claims.quote: JIT protection for Endpoint DLP supports these devices: Windows 10; Windows 11; macOS (the three most recent versions)

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not document whether advanced classification sends content from these RMS-protected files to the cloud classification service.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Endpoint DLP" "RMS" "advanced classification" cloud'. Opened endpoint settings and the diagnostic-log guide. Settings describe general cloud scanning, but the guide says encrypted files cannot be evaluated; neither resolves this new RMS-protected-file case.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure and Security & identity
claims.claim: The roadmap describes classification, not a change to identities or permissions to open protected files.
claims.quote: Endpoint DLP can now classify Office files stored in Windows devices that have Azure RMS protection applied. Classification will be triggered when file is used in applications or when just-in-time classification is enabled.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationales
claims.claim: Device DLP rules can block or block with override egress activities such as USB copy, network-share copy, printing and restricted-cloud uploads.
claims.quote: DLP checks if any DLP rule defines Block or Block with override actions for the attempted activity. If yes, evaluation continues.

claims.claim: Activity explorer shows audited endpoint activity, including sensitive information type details where applicable.
claims.quote: Once a device is onboarded, information about audited activities flows into Activity explorer even before you configure and deploy any DLP policies that have devices as a location.

claims.claim: Files in excluded Windows paths are not audited.
claims.quote: Files in excluded locations aren't audited.

claims.claim: Files created or modified in excluded Windows paths are not subject to DLP policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Any files that you create or modify in those locations aren't subject to DLP policy enforcement.
